title: Training video cost: agency vs in-house vs AI tools
summary: What a training video costs from an agency, an in-house team, or an AI tool, with sourced prices and an estimate for a 20-video onboarding library.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


- Agencies quote per project. Breadnbeyond's animated videos start at $1,000 for one minute, and Wyzowl's survey of 116 production companies found a median quote of $5,400.
- In-house video costs staff time: about $47.58 an hour at the BLS median for training and development specialists plus benefits, and 4–7 hours per short video by hand.
- AI video tools charge a subscription, so most of the remaining cost is time per video. Clueso's paid plans start at $40 a month billed yearly.
- For 20 one-minute videos, that comes to about $20,000–$108,000 with an agency, $4,100–$6,900 in-house, and $800–$3,350 with an AI tool.
- Keeping the videos current after each release is a separate cost that repeats every year.


You've been asked to put a number on 20 onboarding videos, and the figures you can find don't line up. One production company publishes a starting price of $1,000 a video, an industry survey puts the median quote at $5,400, and making them in-house comes with no price tag at all.


Before switching tools, Snappt's team measured what one training video cost them in time: 13–17 hours of scripting, recording, editing, and reviewing. Nobody sends an invoice for those hours, so they rarely appear in a budget next to the agency quote they should be compared with.


This guide puts agency, in-house, and AI-tool production on the same footing. Every figure links to its source, and the worked example shows the arithmetic for a 20-video library so you can swap in your own numbers.


## How much does a training video cost to make?


The cost of a training video is everything it takes to put one finished, accurate video in front of learners: the production fee or staff hours, software, narration and translation, and review time from the people who know the process. An agency puts most of that on one invoice, while an in-house team pays for it in salaried hours that rarely get counted.


Published figures for one short video run from about $190 in staff time to $5,400 at the median agency quote, and format and length move the number further.


## What does a production agency charge for a training video?


Most production companies quote per project after a discovery call, so the public numbers come from the few agencies that list a price and from surveys that collected quotes.


[Breadnbeyond's pricing page](https://www.breadnbeyond.com/pricing/) starts animated videos at $1,000 for a one-minute package, including script, voiceover, and animation, with an extra charge for every 10 seconds past the first minute. Each package takes five weeks or more.[Wyzowl asked 242 explainer video companies](https://wyzowl.com/explainer-video-cost/) to quote for the same 60-second animated video in late 2022. The 116 that gave a price ranged from $600 to $250,000, with a median of $5,400.


[Clutch's video production pricing data](https://clutch.co/agencies/video-production/pricing) , compiled from verified client reviews, puts typical US agency rates at $100–$149 an hour and says most projects come in under $10,000. Its average project cost of $42,280.92 covers every kind of video, so large commercial shoots pull it up.


The published floor and the survey median sit more than five times apart, and both price animated explainers rather than recorded walkthroughs. Neither includes the hours your subject-matter experts spend briefing the agency and reviewing drafts.


## What does it cost to make training videos in-house?


In-house video has no invoice, so its cost is the hours someone spends on it, multiplied by what an hour of their time costs, plus software.


The[BLS puts the median annual wage for training and development specialists](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/training-and-development-specialists.htm) at $69,280 as of May 2025, or $33.31 an hour over a 2,080-hour year. Wages make up 70.0% of private employers' compensation costs in the[BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ecec.nr0.htm) for June 2026, so dividing by 0.70 to add benefits gives a loaded rate of about $47.58.


Three teams published their per-video times from before they switched tools.[Teamworks](https://www.clueso.io/customers/teamworks) spent four to five hours on one short video that passed through four separate tools.[Intellum](https://www.clueso.io/customers/intellum) spent 6–7 hours per video.[Snappt](https://www.clueso.io/customers/snappt) spent 13–17 hours and described it as almost an hour of editing for each minute of video, so longer videos land further up the range.


At 4–7 hours, one short video costs $190–$333 in staff time.[Adobe Premiere](https://www.adobe.com/products/premiere/plans.html) adds $22.99 a month per person on an annual plan. Hiring someone dedicated is the other in-house route: the[BLS median wage for film and video editors](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/media-and-communication/film-and-video-editors-and-camera-operators.htm) is $75,420, or about $107,700 a year with benefits.


## What do AI video tools cost for training videos?


AI video tools charge a subscription by seat and by minutes exported, so the tool costs the same whether you make five videos or 50, up to the export limit. The hours per video are what change.


Clueso's plans make a workable example. The[Free plan](https://www.clueso.io/pricing) exports 10 minutes of video a month with a watermark, and Solo is $40 a month billed yearly for one editor and three hours of exports a year. Business is $120 a month billed yearly for two editors and six hours, plus $40 for each extra editor. Enterprise is priced on request and is the plan with[SCORM export](https://www.clueso.io/features/scorm-export) , in-video quizzes, and branching, which matters if your LMS has to record completions and scores.


Avatar-led tools publish entry plans in a similar range: Synthesia's Starter plan is $19 a month and HeyGen's Creator plan is $29, both billed monthly.


The hours drop because the tool takes over the scripting and narration. You record a rough walkthrough, or start from a[slide deck](https://www.clueso.io/features/ppt-video) , a[PDF](https://www.clueso.io/tools/pdf-to-video-converter) , or a prompt, and Clueso writes the script, reads it with an[AI voiceover](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-voiceovers) , adds zooms, and produces a[step-by-step written guide](https://www.clueso.io/features/help-articles) from the same project. Teamworks now makes a video in 20–30 minutes and Intellum in one to two hours. Those are two customers' figures rather than a benchmark, so time a few of your own before budgeting on them.


> Time your own videos on[Clueso's Free plan](https://www.clueso.io/pricing) .


If you're comparing tools rather than routes, our[guide to training video software](https://www.clueso.io/solutions/training-video-software) covers the main options.

Take a library of 20[onboarding videos](https://www.clueso.io/blog/employee-onboarding-videos-with-examples) , each about a minute long, made once. Every input comes from the sections above, and the table leaves out any cost without a published number.

The agency rows assume no changes after delivery. At Snappt's 13–17 hours a video, the in-house row would reach about $12,600–$16,500.


In cash, the in-house route costs less than the cheapest agency quote, but it takes 80–140 hours, two to three and a half working weeks pulled from the rest of someone's job. An AI tool brings that down to 7–40 hours for less than the staff time it replaces.


## How do you estimate what your own training videos will cost?


Your own figures will hold up better than national medians, and you can collect most of them in a week:


1. **Time one video end to end.** Count from the first draft of the script to the published file, reviews included.
2. **Work out your loaded hourly rate.** Divide the maker's annual salary by 2,080, then divide by 0.70 to add benefits.
3. **Get one written quote for the same script.** Ask what's included, how many revision rounds, and what a change costs after delivery.
4. **Price a year of tools.** Include every subscription the work touches, from the editor to the voiceover tool.
5. **Multiply by the library, then add updates.** Use this year's video count, plus the cost of keeping them current.


For in-house and AI tools, the sum is **videos × hours per video × loaded hourly rate, plus a year of tools, plus updates** . For an agency, it's **videos × the quote, plus your review hours × loaded hourly rate, plus updates** .


## What does it cost to keep training videos up to date?


Most budgets plan only for the first version. Each release that moves a screen sends some videos back for a fix, and an in-house team re-records them unless its tool lets it[edit the script and replace only the clip that changed](https://www.clueso.io/blog/update-training-video-without-re-recording) . With an agency, ask before you sign what an update costs six months after delivery.


We worked through the numbers in[why maintaining product videos now costs more than making them](https://www.clueso.io/blog/product-video-maintenance-cost) : a 200-video library where four releases a year each touch 40 videos needs 160 fixes, or 640–800 hours a year if each is re-recorded by hand. That line comes back every year the videos stay in use, so put your own version of it in the estimate.


If the total is going to finance, our guide to[building a business case for video creation software](https://www.clueso.io/blog/business-case-for-video-creation-software) covers how to present it. Before that, time the next training video your team makes, from first script to published file, and ask one agency to quote the same script. Those two numbers, multiplied by the size of your library, will be closer to your real cost than any range in this post.


## Frequently asked questions


### How much does it cost to produce a training video in-house versus with an agency?


In-house, a short video costs about $190–$333 in staff time, at 4–7 hours and the BLS median wage for training specialists plus benefits. Agency prices start around $1,000 for a one-minute animated video, with a survey median of $5,400.[Clueso's paid plans](https://www.clueso.io/pricing) start at $40 a month billed yearly, and Teamworks makes a video in 20–30 minutes.


### How do we build the business case for an AI video tool for our training team?


Compare what one video costs today in hours and loaded hourly rate with the subscription plus the hours the same video takes in the new tool. Test on real videos from your backlog; Clueso's[Free plan](https://www.clueso.io/pricing) is enough to time a handful. Our guide to[building a business case for video creation software](https://www.clueso.io/blog/business-case-for-video-creation-software) covers presenting the result.


### Is it cheaper to hire a video editor or use an agency for training videos?


A video editor at the BLS median wage costs about $107,700 a year with benefits, roughly what 20 videos cost at the $5,400 median agency quote. If the editor makes more than 20 videos a year, the hire costs less per video; for a handful a year, the agency does. A third option is an AI video tool for the people who already own the training: in Clueso they record or prompt the video, and the script and[AI voiceover](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-voiceovers) are generated for them.


### What hidden costs should I budget for in training video production?


Budget separately for subject-matter expert review time, translation, LMS packaging, and updates after the product or process changes, because none of them show up in a per-video quote or an hourly rate. Each language adds its own narration and captions, which every later update has to repeat. Clueso[translates the voiceover, captions, and written guide into 150+ languages](https://www.clueso.io/features/auto-translate) on every plan, and SCORM export is on the Enterprise plan.


### Can an AI video tool replace a production agency for training videos?


For most training videos, yes: software walkthroughs, process and policy training, onboarding, and explainers. Clueso builds these from a screen recording, a prompt, a slide deck, or a PDF, and adds[motion graphics](https://www.clueso.io/features/motion-graphics) for the parts that are clearer illustrated. An agency still earns its fee when the video needs filmed footage of your own people and places, such as a safety walkthrough of your warehouse.
